pages.title: Conclusion
pages.text:
Conclusion
A comfortable building does not “cool the body” by one mechanism only; it manages air temperature, surface
temperature, humidity and air movement so that the four heat-exchange paths remain physiologically manageable .

Thermal comfort is the condition in which a person feels thermally satisfied and the body can maintain heat balance
without excessive physiological effort such as heavy sweating or shivering.

Subjective / individual variables
      Clothing
      Acclimatization
      Age and sex

 Data note for 2023
 The 2023 paper clearly states a 45×25×3 m room. It differs from the 45×23×3 m room used in 2021 and 2022, so it is
 calculated separately rather than forced into the earlier dimensions.

Workflow: V = L×B×H → air-space/person = V/N → choose the non-smoking rate from the course table → Qtotal =
rate×N → convert L/s to m³/s → ACH = Q×3600/V.

2021 solution - 200 persons
V = 45×23×3 = 3105 m³. Air-space/person = 3105/200 = 15.525 m³. The table ends at 12 m³/person, so use the highest
listed non-smoking rate = 6.0 L/s/person (same convention used in the uploaded Section A class note).

                                  Q = 200 × 6.0 = 1200 L/s = 1.20 m³/s

                                  ACH = 1.20 × 3600 / 3105 = 1.39 h⁻¹

2022 solution - 150 persons
Air-space/person = 3105/150 = 20.70 m³ → use 12 m³ table bracket → 6.0 L/s/person.

                                   Q = 150 × 6.0 = 900 L/s = 0.90 m³/s

                                  ACH = 0.90 × 3600 / 3105 = 1.04 h⁻¹

2023 solution - 180 persons
V = 45×25×3 = 3375 m³. Air-space/person = 3375/180 = 18.75 m³ → use the highest listed 12 m³ bracket → 6.0
L/s/person.

                                  Q = 180 × 6.0 = 1080 L/s = 1.08 m³/s

Higher altitude - exam-safe explanation

so being closer to the sun is not the controlling effect.

Rat-trap bond is a brick masonry technique in which bricks are placed on edge/vertical orientation so that a
continuous cavity is formed within the wall thickness. The cavity reduces material use and improves thermal and
acoustic resistance when the wall is properly detailed.

                                       Rat-trap bond - cavity formed within a nominal brick-wall thickness.

Construction rules
      Use consistent good-quality bricks; dimensional variation affects the bond.
      Keep bottom/top closure courses and opening jamb/sill/lintel zones solid where required .
      Maintain the cavity without excessive mortar droppings bridging it.
      Provide reinforcement/bands/corner detailing where structural design or seismic requirements demand it .
      Plan services carefully so the cavity is not unintentionally destroyed.

Advantages
      Lower brick and mortar use; the lecture slide reports approximately 25% fewer bricks and 40% less mortar
       than conventional masonry in one comparison.

                                    Seasonal migration of the ITCZ - conceptual annual shift around the equator.

The Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) is the equatorial/sub-equatorial belt where the NE and SE trade winds
converge. Warm moist air rises, so surface horizontal wind can be weak, variable and calm - the traditional
“doldrums”.

Why it shifts
      The zone of maximum solar heating migrates north and south with the apparent seasonal movement of the sun .
      ITCZ follows this thermal low, moving northward in northern summer and southward in northern winter .
      It often migrates farther north over the Northern Hemisphere because there is more land , and land heats more
       strongly/quickly than ocean in summer, pulling the thermal low northward.

Effects of the annual shift
      Seasonal reversal/shift of prevailing winds.
      Monsoon circulation and seasonal rainfall migration.
      Changes in cloud, humidity and storm activity.
      Important seasonal design changes in ventilation and rain protection.

2021: protective measures in warm-humid climate
      Provide maximum ventilation and air movement with large, well-positioned openings.
      Provide maximum shading against both direct and diffuse solar radiation.
      Avoid unnecessary heat storage; favour light construction where appropriate.
      Use reflective/light-coloured outer surfaces and well-insulated, ventilated double roofs .
      Use vegetation for shade and microclimate moderation without blocking useful breezes .

Hot-dry desert: why it forms and why day-night range is large
      Around 20-30° latitude, descending air in the subtropical high suppresses cloud formation and rainfall .
      Clear skies allow intense daytime solar heating and strong night-time long-wave radiation .
      Low humidity and sparse vegetation mean little latent-heat buffering; surfaces heat and cool rapidly.

Hot-dry building precautions
      Use compact form and mutual shading to reduce exposed surface area.
      Use thick/heavy envelope where useful to exploit thermal mass and time lag.
      Keep openings small/controlled during hot dusty periods; use protected night ventilation when outdoor air
       becomes cooler.
      Shade roofs, walls and openings; use light/reflective external surfaces.
      Use courtyard and evaporative cooling where water availability permits.
      Protect against dust and sand infiltration with screens, vestibules and careful detailing.

The uploaded site-climate slide lists temperature inversion as a deviation factor but does not fully define its
mechanism. Standard meteorological meaning: a temperature inversion occurs when temperature increases with
height over a layer instead of normally decreasing. Cool dense air can be trapped near the ground beneath warmer
air.

Typical causes / example
      Night-time radiative cooling of ground under clear calm conditions can cool the near-surface air.
      Cold air can drain into valleys/depressions and become trapped.
      A warm layer above suppresses vertical mixing, allowing fog/smog and pollutants to accumulate .
    Exam caution
    Do not claim “global warming causes all inversions”. Treat inversion as a vertical/local atmospheric structure that can
    intensify urban pollution/thermal discomfort; the question wording “from the perspective of global warming” can be
    answered by discussing its interaction with urban heat/pollution rather than a direct one-to-one cause.

Atmospheric pressure is the force per unit area exerted by the weight of the air column above a surface . In moist air
